title: Blueprint for graceful weight swap and preload gates
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a low-risk, incremental plan to reduce cold-start variance and simplify tokenizer/weights coupling by introducing a staged weight hydration flow and 'preload gates' that make model asset activation observable and interruptible. The goal is not to change on-disk formats immediately but to create a stable orchestration layer that can swallow future format and sharding changes with minimal client-visible disruption.

Problem background:
- We currently see significant tail variance during model bootstrap when large shards are fetched and tokenizers initialize concurrently. On p3-like infra, 95th percentile model-ready time for Llama-2/13B artifacts varies between ~1.2s and 6.8s depending on shard layout and tokenizer cold-cache.
- Tokenizer init logic is entangled with the weight loader in several places (vocab detection, tokenizer policy negotiation), making it risky to change weight shard ordering or to swap in quantized shards without touching tokenizer codepaths.
- Existing lazy-activation approach is brittle: partial hydration leaves the runtime in multiple intermediate states and complicates rollback on failure.

Proposal (high level):
1) Two-phase loader: metadata-only manifest scan (fast), followed by background hydration phases controlled by explicit preload gates (critical, non-critical).
2) Atomic weight swap API: allow the runtime to prepare an alternate memory-mapped weight set and commit it with a single switch-over operation so in-flight requests observe either old or new weights.
3) Outboard tokenizer handshake: move tokenizer fingerprinting and minimal vocab probe to a small sidecar service (tokenizer-prober) so heavy tokenizer construction can be done asynchronously and validated before the model becomes fully routable.
4) Health & metrics: introduce fine-grained metrics (hydrate_bytes_in_progress, commit_latency_ms, tokenizer_probe_status) and a short-lived guard that rejects traffic if commit_latency exceeds SLA.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Backwards compatibility: We keep existing on-disk weight formats and sharding rules for now; the orchestration layer will support format adapters in a follow-up ticket. This minimizes customer risk and allows shipping quickly.
- Complexity vs safety: The atomic swap requires careful memory management, and we accept a modest runtime memory overhead during transition windows in exchange for dramatically simpler rollback semantics.
- Tokenizer sidecar increases components to operate, but decoupling reduces cross-team coupling and enables tokenizer-specific caching strategies (e.g., disk-backed vocab cache) without changing the serving runtime.

Acceptance criteria:
- Loader exposes a /ready-state endpoint indicating phases: manifest-scanned, seeds-hydrated, critical-shards-committed, tokenizer-probed, fully-routable.
- Demonstrate 30% reduction in 95th percentile model-ready times on benchmark suite compared to baseline measured 2025-01-05.
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate partial hydration failures and validate rollback path.
- Document atomic swap API in runtime developer guide and publish migration notes for downstream teams.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (experimental branch): implement manifest scan + simple preload gate and tokenizer-prober sidecar behind a feature flag. Run perf job on canary fleet for 2 weeks. (Owners: Diego, Alexandra).
- Phase B (validation): add atomic swap path and metrics, expand canary to 10% traffic, run chaos tests (network partitions, out-of-order shard arrival).
- Phase C (full): turn on by default for new model loads, add telemetry dashboards and incident playbook.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Blueprint+for+Graceful+Weight+Swap
- Benchmark dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/model-load/cold-start-2025
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4820
- Tokenizer prober repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer-prober (initial prototype branch: feature/preload-gates)
